| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tool | `kailash verifier` (d-07 CLI) + D-7 toolkit packs |
| Section | Administrator |
| Level | medium |
| Time | ~30 min |
| Layer/Category | DEFENCE / d-07-standards-verification |
| Tags | `admin`, `verifier`, `aisvs`, `mlsvs`, `owasp-llm-top10`, `evidence` |


## Problem

Your lab ran (say) a scoped garak scan or an attack-then-verify pair
run, and the report's finding says "mitigated" or "observed". To mean
anything in front of an auditor, a risk owner, or an authorisation
review, that claim has to land on a NAMED control in a NAMED standard at
a NAMED verification level — and the mapping from what you actually ran
to the control statement has to be generated from the same manifest
that shipped the tool, not hand-appealed in a slide. The D-7 verifier is
the CLI that renders that mapping.

## Solution

Pick the standard, run the verifier slice, bind the run evidence to the
control rows it renders:

```bash
# 0. Confirm your lab surface ran at ALL (the input to any mapping):
#    e.g. [Attack the platform, then verify](../attack-defence/attack-then-verify.html)
#    leaves a --record JSON (real, verbatim-backed); a garak run leaves a
#    .jsonl report. A control statement without run evidence is a wish.

# 1. The LLM-side OWASP maps (both Top-10 epochs live in the manifest):
kailash verifier --standard llm-top10
#    -> the LLM Top 10 evidence view driven by the llm-top10-toolkit row
#       (risk-mapping data for 2026 + v2:2025 epochs)

# 2. The AI-security verification standard, per level:
kailash verifier --standard aisvs --level 2
#    -> AISVS 1.0 requirements at verification level 2 — the landed
#       example shape (spec §2.8's standard-first mode; Phase-6's
#       acceptance ran exactly this)

# 3. The ML-system sibling standard:
kailash verifier --standard mlsvs
#    -> MLSVS checklist view from the mlsvs-toolkit row

# 4. Bind the run: cite the run's artefact against the standard rows in
#    your report — the verifier's output IS the citation skeleton:
#      "control <row-id> (AISVS 1.0, level 2): verified by
#       garak --spec tag:owasp:llm01 (report <file>, tool pin <rev>),
#       target <endpoint>, recorded <date>"
#    the manifest-driven rows make this citable; the run record makes it
#    REPRODUCIBLE; the tool pin in the row's record makes it
#    RE-RUNNABLE.

# 5. Sanity: the same facts from the manifest's own view
kailash info garak | grep -i -A4 owasp
#    -> the row's owasp_llm map (2026 + v2 epochs) — what the verifier
#       renders for LLM-top10 rows in the first place
```

Expected output shape (abridged):

```
$ kailash verifier --standard aisvs --level 2
standard: aisvs  version: 1.0
level: 2
<section>:
  <requirement-id>  verify that ...   <- the tool rows whose
      evidence: <tool-id> <tactic/map refs>     manifest maps to it
...
```

What success looks like:

- the verifier's standard/level line names the OWASP stack exactly as
  the spec's standard-first mode promises (ASVS 5.0 / AISVS 1.0 /
  MLSVS / LLM Top 10, both epochs)
- every rendered row traces back to a manifest field (`owasp_llm`,
  `atlas_tactics`, the D-7 toolkit rows' mapping data) — no hand-copied
  control text anywhere
- your report's citation names: the standard + level, the tool + pin,
  the run record, the date — all four, or the claim is unfinished
- `kailash manifest validate` stays green (the mapping's ground truth
  is the same manifest the CLI bakes)

## Discussion

- **The D-7 shape, one file per concern:** three toolkit rows
  (`aisvs-1.0-toolkit`, `mlsvs-toolkit`, `llm-top10-toolkit` — the
  first-party OWASP mapping packs, status: data) + the verifier CLI
  (`kailash-verifier`, bespoke, BSD-3-Clause) + the ASVS toolkit shared
  with C-10. AISVS/MLSVS/LLM-Top-10 mapping DATA comes from those packs;
  the manifest's per-tool `owasp_llm`/`atlas_tactics` fields are the
  per-tool views the verifier joins against them. AISVS levels carry
  the ASVS alignment (level N verifies at matching ASVS level N — the
  AI chapters and the web chapters are applied TOGETHER per upstream).
- **Three navigation modes, one manifest** (spec §2.8): menu is
  layer-first; the ATLAS matrix is tactic-first; the standards view is
  standard-first — the verifier is that third mode made runnable from
  the CLI. One record, three views, no separate "compliance copy"
  anywhere to drift.
- **What a verified control statement looks like:** a row-id + a
  mechanism + run-reproduction. "AISVS 1.0 §<chapter/id> level 2 —
  verified by <tool> <version> against <target/record> on <date>" —
  with the record itself attached (a garak JSONL, an mlflow-pair
  --record JSON). The book's no-invented-evidence rule is the same
  discipline standards-mapped: a claim with no verbatim-run behind it
  is not evidence.
- **Level choice is a posture decision, not a decoration:** AISVS
  levels are ascending depth-of-assurance per requirement (level 1 =
  the critical/foundational controls, level 3 = defence-in-depth /
  niche). Pick the level your AUTHORISATION context demands (e.g.
  IRAP/ISM-mapped work will want the higher levels evidenced, not
  just level 1) and STATE the level in every downstream citation —
  the `--level N` flag is part of the claim, not a knob.
- **LLM Top 10 has two epochs and the manifest carries both:** the
  owasp_llm field maps both `{2026: ...}` and `{v2: ...}` per row — a
  report that names only one epoch is incomplete for any audience that
  spans the v2:2025 → 2026 transition; the verifier's llm-top10 view
  renders them as the toolkit's dual-epoch data says.
- **NIST/ISO coverage lives in D-6; the verifier binds D-7 evidence:**
  ISO/IEC 42001 (AIMS), NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act inventories and
  questionnaires are the D-6 governance pack's rows (see
  [Govern a GenAI vendor with the D-6 pack](govern-vendor-review.html)) —
  the D-7 verifier's job is the TECHNICAL verification leg those
  frameworks then consume. Don't conflate them: regulation asks for
  control evidence; the verifier produces the control mapping that the
  evidence cites.
- **What the verifier does NOT do:** it maps and renders; it does not
  RUN the tool for you or mint a pass. The verdict discipline of the
  book applies inside the mapping too — evidence first, then the
  statement, never the reverse.
